problem:
A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-24t+8$ meters per second.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $5\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)={t}^{4}-150{t}^{2}+8$ meters.
Calculate the time at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude.
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration. 

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-150{t}^{2}+8) \\  & =4{t}^{3}-300t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-300t) \\  & =12{t}^{2}-300\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}12{t}^{2}-300 & =0 \\ 12{t}^{2} & =300 \\ {t}^{2} & =25 \\ t & =\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at $t=5\,\text{s}.$
